package_info.package_manager: standalone binary (Golang malware, not a package manager ecosystem)
package_info.why_malicious: Skuld is a purpose-built information stealer written in Golang, designed to exfiltrate sensitive data from infected systems, including credentials, browser data, Discord tokens, system information, and potentially cryptocurrency assets. It uses multiple exfiltration channels (Discord webhooks, Gofile), anti-analysis techniques, and targets a wide range of applications and files, making it a clear example of malicious software.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Searches for and reads data from Discord application folders, browser credential stores (e.g., masterkey_db, login_db, download_db, history_db, card_db), and system folders.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code enumerates and reads sensitive files from Discord, web browsers, and user/system directories, then prepares this data for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Legitimate software does not indiscriminately access credential stores, browser databases, or Discord tokens without user consent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications only access their own data or user-approved files, not credential stores or unrelated application data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensics or backup tools may access browser data with explicit user permission.
key_indicators: Access to Discord tokens and application data
Enumeration of sensitive files and folders

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Sends exfiltrated data to hardcoded Discord webhooks (e.g., https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...) and/or Gofile upload endpoints (https://api.gofile.io/getServer, gofile.io/uploadFile).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code transmits collected sensitive data to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks and/or Gofile servers via HTTPS POST requests.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating sensitive data to external web services, especially Discord webhooks and anonymous file sharing services, is a hallmark of information stealers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not send user credentials or private data to external, hardcoded endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Bug reporting tools may send logs to a developer's server, but never credentials or tokens.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhooks for exfiltration
Use of Gofile API for file upload

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Performs system checks to detect virtualization, sandboxes, or debugging environments (e.g., checking for known VM artifacts, registry keys, or process names).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code inspects the environment for signs of virtualization or analysis tools, and may alter its behavior or terminate if detected.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Anti-analysis and sandbox evasion are common in malware to avoid detection and analysis.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely checks for virtualization or debuggers unless for licensing or support reasons.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some commercial software may check for VMs to prevent piracy.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Captures clipboard data and/or takes screenshots of the user's desktop.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code reads clipboard contents and/or captures screenshots, then includes this data in the exfiltration payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Capturing clipboard and screen data is a classic data theft technique, especially when combined with credential or session theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not capture clipboard or screen data without explicit user action.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote support tools may capture screens with user consent.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Searches for and attempts to access cryptocurrency wallet files or modules (feature in development).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code attempts to locate and access files or modules related to cryptocurrency wallets, potentially to steal wallet data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Targeting cryptocurrency wallets is a high-value theft behavior, not expected in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not access or search for unrelated wallet files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cryptocurrency management tools may access wallet files, but only with user consent.

attack_chain.action: Malware is executed on the victim's system (user runs malicious EXE).
Performs anti-analysis checks to evade sandboxes and debuggers.
Enumerates and collects sensitive data: Discord tokens, browser credentials, system info, clipboard, screenshots, and (optionally) cryptocurrency wallets.
Exfiltrates collected data to attacker-controlled Discord webhooks and/or Gofile servers.

behavioral_signatures: Golang binary accessing browser credential stores and Discord application data
Network connections to Discord webhooks and Gofile API endpoints
Clipboard and screen capture activity by unknown processes
Anti-analysis checks (VM, sandbox, debugger detection) in userland binaries
file_indicators: Presence of browser database file access (e.g., masterkey_db, login_db, download_db, history_db, card_db)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTPS POST requests to https://discord.com/api/webhooks/*
Outbound requests to https://api.gofile.io/getServer and gofile.io/uploadFile
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unknown Golang binaries accessing browser credential stores, Discord application data, or cryptocurrency wallet files. Flag processes making outbound HTTPS requests to Discord webhooks or Gofile endpoints, especially if preceded by credential or clipboard access. Detect anti-analysis routines by monitoring for system checks indicative of sandbox or debugger evasion. Correlate file access patterns with network exfiltration to identify information stealer activity.
